hints: Focus on the two stages in order, first addition to the carbonyl, then hydrolysis of what is formed.
Propanone is $(CH_3)_2C=O$, so its cyanohydrin adds both $OH$ and $CN$ to the same carbonyl carbon to give $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CN$.
Remember that acidic hydrolysis converts the $CN$ group fully to $COOH$, while the $OH$ already present stays unchanged.
walkthrough:
**Form the cyanohydrin from propanone**

Propanone is a ketone, so HCN adds across its C=O bond. Both new groups end up on the same carbon.

$$ (CH_3)_2C=O + HCN \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(OH)CN $$

**Hydrolyse the nitrile under acidic conditions**

A nitrile group, $CN$, is hydrolysed by hot aqueous acid to a carboxylic acid group, $COOH$. This is a full hydrolysis, not a partial one.

$$ R-CN + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow R-COOH + NH_4^+ $$

**Apply this to our cyanohydrin**

Here $R$ is $(CH_3)_2C(OH)$, so the $CN$ becomes $COOH$ and the $OH$ is untouched.

$$ (CH_3)_2C(OH)CN + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(OH)COOH + NH_4^+ $$

**Identify the final product**

The final molecule has two $CH_3$ groups, one $OH$ and one $COOH$ all on the same central carbon. That matches 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanoic acid.

options.A: This is $CH_3CH(OH)COOH$, the product you would get starting from ethanal, not propanone. It has only one $CH_3$ group, so the carbon skeleton is too small.
options.B: This is butanoic acid, $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$, which has no $OH$ group. The cyanohydrin route always keeps an $OH$ on the same carbon as the new acid group, so this cannot form.
options.C: This is an amide, $(CH_3)_2CHCONH_2$. Amides form by partial hydrolysis of nitriles, but hot acidic hydrolysis goes all the way to the carboxylic acid. Also the $OH$ group is missing here.
options.D: This is $(CH_3)_2C(OH)COOH$. The cyanohydrin $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CN$ is formed first, then acidic hydrolysis changes $CN$ to $COOH$ while leaving the $OH$ and the two $CH_3$ groups in place.
